top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection) is the mature, clearly identified discovery whose central claim, that selection and reallocation across firms shape the gains from trade, has been tested repeatedly on firm-level data from many countries for more than twenty years. I weigh repeated confrontation with real data most heavily, as in my own contract-based work. Melitz (2003) is the originating model, and Helpman's joint work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI is part of the same framework. The framework is distinct from the 2008 prize, which covered representative-firm theory of intra-industry trade and location. The citation should be worded around the theoretical framework, not all firm-level trade research. The omission of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum is a real attribution cost that I do not think justifies waiting. P003 (Kiyotaki-Moore) is a close second. It is a clean two-author mechanism that is distinct from the 2022 prize, but its collateral channel is identified less cleanly empirically than the theory. P002 ranks third because its credit is spread over eight names and a three-person cut is contestable, although its policy footprint is large. P000 is last because all three proposals are substantive and mature. I have not independently verified citations or priority claims.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for B026, B007 or B012. No co-authorship or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman, Kiyotaki, Moore, Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. Disclosed: adjunct position at Chicago Booth, KVA vice-presidency, earlier committee service including as chair 2016-2018, and SSE affiliation shared with some other members. My field of corporate finance is closest to B001, which is not among the proposals. These ties are disclosed, not adjudicated.
